title: Launch Brief (Draft): Guided Onboarding + First Production Launch Checklist (Hosted API, Console)
content:
Doc purpose
This is a working launch brief for the Guided Onboarding + “First Production Launch” checklist for Hosted API users, delivered as an in-Console checklist experience backed by onboarding eventing + progress tracking. This document is intended to align Product, Console, DevEx, Telemetry, Support/CS, and SRE on target audience, rollout, success metrics, comms, and readiness.

TL;DR
- What’s launching: A new checklist entry point in Redwood Console that makes required onboarding + first production steps explicit (API key, first request, streaming, retries/timeouts, usage dashboard, quotas/budgets, model pinning, fallback policy, basic observability hooks). Checklist progress is computed from reliable server-side onboarding events (plus limited client hints).
- Why now: Reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) and time-to-first-production-traffic (TTFP), increase activation/retention, and reduce top onboarding support tickets (401/403, rate-limit surprises, streaming disconnect confusion, usage dashboard lag confusion).
- How we’ll roll out: Feature-flagged; internal dogfood -> limited new-tenant cohort -> progressive rollout by cohort with regression alerts + kill switch.

Launch name (internal)
“Console Onboarding Checklist (Hosted API MVP)”

Customer-facing framing (working copy)
“Get to production faster with a guided onboarding checklist in the Redwood Console.”

Scope (MVP)
Included:
- Console checklist UI/UX: checklist component, step detail drawer, deep links into Console pages/docs, step states (Not started / In progress / Complete / Needs attention where applicable), error/empty states, accessibility pass.
- Progress tracking service: persisted checklist state and derived completion based on onboarding events; admin overrides for Support/CS with audit trail.
- Eventing: standardized onboarding event schema v1; primary emission from gateway/control plane (server-side) for reliability.
- Docs + quickstarts updates: canonical checklist docs page + “production readiness” quickstart updates to mirror steps; SDK production defaults guidance (timeouts/retries/streaming reconnect patterns).
- Telemetry/KPIs: dashboards for TTFS/TTFP and funnel; alerts for regressions and data freshness.

Explicitly not in MVP:
- Full in-product guided tours (walkthrough overlays)
- Private deployment onboarding wizard
- Automated remediation suggestions (e.g., “you are hitting 429; click to apply backoff config”)

Target audience
Primary (MVP):
- New self-serve Hosted API tenants (PLG motion) who have created an account but have not yet shipped production traffic.
- Devs evaluating Redwood who get stuck on common onboarding issues: auth/key setup, streaming robustness, rate limits/quotas, and understanding usage/cost.

Secondary:
- Existing Hosted API tenants who are increasing usage and need “production readiness” guardrails (quotas/budget alerts, model pinning, fallbacks).
- Sales-assisted prospects who request a “launch checklist” for internal approvals (security + readiness narrative). Note: Enterprise/Dedicated/Private are not primary targets for this MVP but the language should not exclude them.

Non-goals for launch messaging (keep narrow):
- Do not position as a compliance artifact (“certification”) or guarantee of performance.
- Do not imply the checklist is exhaustive for all production requirements; it’s a starter set.

Key user problems this launch is meant to solve
1) “I signed up but can’t get a successful API call.”
   - Frequent 401/403 from wrong env var, wrong key, wrong org/project context.
2) “I got streaming working once but it breaks / disconnects and I’m not sure what to do.”
   - Confusion around reconnect patterns, timeouts, and partial responses.
3) “We launched and immediately hit 429 or quota limits.”
   - Users don’t understand quotas, rate limits, burst behavior, or how to implement retries/backoff.
4) “The usage dashboard doesn’t match what I’m seeing.”
   - Dashboard lag/data freshness confusion; unclear where to look for canonical usage.
5) “How do I make this safer for production?”
   - Model pinning, fallback policy, basic observability hooks, cost controls.

What the user will see (Console UX summary)
Entry points (MVP):
- New Console home / project overview page: “Get started” module with checklist progress.
- Banner / CTA for eligible cohorts: “Finish setup for production readiness” (exact placement per Console UX spec).

Checklist behavior:
- Steps are shown in a recommended order; each step has:
  - One-line description (very short)
  - “Why it matters” and “How to complete” (concise)
  - Deep links to Console pages (API keys, usage, quotas) and to canonical docs/quickstarts
- Step completion is primarily event-driven (server-side events). Some steps may be completed by explicit UI action (e.g., “Viewed usage dashboard”) but we should bias toward durable signals.
- If data is missing/late: show “We’re still syncing activity (up to X minutes)” rather than falsely implying failure.

MVP step set (working; aligns to template)
Onboarding / first success:
1) Create an API key (Console deep link)
2) Set environment variable / secret correctly (docs + troubleshooting)
3) Make your first successful request (2xx) (quickstart deep link + code snippets)
4) Try streaming (and understand disconnect behavior) (docs + examples)

Production readiness:
5) Add production-safe client settings (timeouts + retries/backoff; idempotency guidance where applicable)
6) Review usage & costs in Console (usage dashboard; note data latency expectations)
7) Set quotas and/or budget alerts (Console + Terraform snippet where relevant)
8) Pin a model version for production (Console config)
9) Configure a fallback policy (if supported for Hosted API tier; otherwise doc the recommended pattern)
10) Add basic observability hooks (request IDs, structured logging, tracing hooks; links to docs)

Rollout plan (feature-flagged)
Feature flag name (working): onboarding_checklist_console_v1
Owner: Marissa Cole / Dylan Brooks (Console) + Logan Wright (Telemetry) for measurement

Cohorts:
Phase 0: Internal dogfood
- Audience: Redwood employees only (internal tenants)
- Goal: Validate step order, deep links, event correctness, and eliminate regressions (race conditions/out-of-order events)
- Exit criteria:
  - No critical bugs in step state progression
  - Admin override tool validated by Support
  - Dashboard shows consistent funnel for dogfood cohort

Phase 1: Limited external (new tenants only)
- Audience: New Hosted API signups only (exclude existing tenants initially to reduce confusion)
- Target: 5% of new tenants for 3–5 days
- Exclusions: enterprise-managed tenants that have custom onboarding flows (as defined by Ben Carter / lifecycle rules)
- Monitoring: TTFS/TTFP deltas, step funnel, support ticket spikes, event pipeline freshness

Phase 2: Expand cohort
- 25% of new tenants for 1 week
- Then 50% if stable

Phase 3: General availability for new tenants
- 100% new tenants
- Consider exposing to existing tenants later via banner/Console module (separate comms)

Kill switch / rollback criteria
Immediate kill switch if any of the following occurs:
- Data quality regression: >15% drop in observed “first successful request” events for new tenants compared to baseline, not explained by traffic drop
- Console errors: checklist module causing elevated Console error rates or degraded load times
- Support impact: >20% week-over-week increase in onboarding-related tickets attributable to checklist confusion
- Privacy/security concern raised by Security review (PII in payloads, unexpected fields)

Success metrics (how we’ll know it worked)
North Star outcomes:
- Reduce median TTFS (signup -> first successful 2xx request) for eligible cohorts
- Reduce median TTFP (signup -> first production traffic) for eligible cohorts

Activation funnel (step completion):
- API key created
- Env var configured correctly (proxy signal; see open questions)
- First 2xx request
- First streaming response established
- Usage dashboard visited
- Quota/budget configured
- Model pinned
- Fallback policy configured

Support outcomes:
- Reduction in top onboarding ticket categories (Q1 baseline):
  - 401/403 “invalid API key” during quickstart
  - 429 rate-limit surprise after initial launch
  - Streaming disconnect confusion
  - Usage dashboard lag/mismatch confusion

Measurement notes / definitions
(Owner: Chris Osei + Mei Lin; final definitions tracked in PM-751)
- TTFS definition (working): time from tenant_created_at to first hosted_api_request_success (2xx) excluding internal tenants; validated against usage/billing tables.
- TTFP definition (working): time from tenant_created_at to “production traffic” threshold (e.g., sustained requests over N minutes and/or token volume threshold); details TBD.
- Attribution: Primary based on server-side events emitted at gateway/control plane; supplement with SDK user-agent tags for onboarding flows.

Go/No-Go checklist (launch readiness)
Product/UX
- [ ] Step copy finalized (brevity, tone, “why it matters”) and reviewed by Design (Tessa Morgan / Kenji Nakamura)
- [ ] Deep links verified across roles/permissions (viewer/editor/admin) and across Console nav variants
- [ ] Empty/error states implemented (“no data yet”, “syncing”, “can’t load progress”)

Engineering
- [ ] Feature flag cohort logic validated (including exclusions)
- [ ] Out-of-order event handling verified (monotonic step transitions; idempotency keys)
- [ ] Admin override endpoints gated to Support/CS roles; audit logging enabled
- [ ] Backfill plan confirmed for pre-launch baselines (ENG-5844 / PR-28475)

Telemetry/Analytics
- [ ] Onboarding KPI dashboard live (TTFS/TTFP + funnel) and validated for dogfood cohort
- [ ] Data freshness alert configured (pipeline lag)
- [ ] Regression alerts configured (funnel drop-offs; unexpected event volume changes)

Security/Compliance
- [ ] Telemetry payloads confirmed PII-free; retention and residency constraints documented
- [ ] Review completed for any new fields in event schema and progress service storage

Docs/DevEx
- [ ] Checklist canonical docs page published and linked from Console steps
- [ ] Quickstart(s) updated to match step order (Python/TS/Go parity)
- [ ] SDK “production defaults” guidance published (timeouts/retries/streaming reconnect)

Support/CS
- [ ] Support macros drafted and validated against checklist states
- [ ] Triage playbook updated (how to interpret step state; where to check event logs)
- [ ] Escalation paths confirmed (Console vs Telemetry vs Platform)
- [ ] Known issues list prepared (dashboard lag; streaming edge cases) with standard language

Internal comms plan
Goals:
- Ensure Support/CS can troubleshoot using checklist state and admin override.
- Ensure Sales/SEs can demo the checklist and set correct expectations.
- Ensure Engineering knows where to look for dashboards/alerts and how to respond to regressions.

Channels + artifacts
- #product announcement: launch summary + who it’s for + key links
- #support enablement post: macros + triage questions + escalation routing
- #devex + #docs: doc links and quickstart parity status
- #eng-platform + #console: eventing/progress service operational notes and on-call pointers
- Release notes entry (Soojin Lee): “Console Guided Onboarding Checklist” with feature-flag note

Suggested internal message (draft)
“We’re rolling out a new Console onboarding checklist for new Hosted API tenants. It’s feature-flagged and starts with internal dogfood, then 5% of new signups. The checklist progress is derived from server-side onboarding events, and Support has an admin override tool for troubleshooting. KPI dashboards (TTFS/TTFP + funnel) are live; please report any copy confusion, broken deep links, or step state inconsistencies.”

Support readiness checklist (operational)
Support should be able to answer:
- Customer sees 401/403: How do we confirm which key they’re using and what env var name is expected? What’s the fastest fix?
- Customer sees 429: Where do they see current quota/rate limits? What are recommended backoff settings per SDK?
- Customer says “streaming disconnect”: What’s expected behavior? How do they safely reconnect? Are they behind a proxy?
- Customer says “usage doesn’t show”: What’s the expected dashboard delay? Where is the canonical usage record? How to explain without undermining trust?

Tools + access
- Checklist admin override: who has access, how to use it, and how actions are audited
- How to view checklist event history (or derived state) for a tenant
- Where to find the onboarding KPI dashboard and how to filter by cohort/flag

Macro snippets (draft; for Support to finalize)
1) 401/403 during quickstart
- Ask: “Which SDK/language? Are you setting REDWOOD_API_KEY (or the key name in docs) in the same environment where your process runs?”
- Provide: link to API key + env var docs, include troubleshooting list.

2) 429 / rate limit surprise
- Ask: “Can you share approximate QPS and token sizes? Are you retrying on 429 with exponential backoff and jitter?”
- Provide: link to quota page and SDK retry defaults guidance.

3) Streaming disconnects
- Ask: “Are you behind a corporate proxy / load balancer? Are you handling read timeouts? Do you need resume semantics?”
- Provide: link to streaming reconnect guidance + example repo.

Customer-facing comms plan (MVP)
No broad external marketing for MVP. Console is the primary surface.
Optional (later): short docs blog post or changelog entry once rolled out to 100% of new tenants and metrics are stable.

Risks / watchouts
- Event ordering/race conditions can cause steps to regress (already seen in dogfood). Must keep monotonic transitions and idempotency.
- Over-instrumentation or ambiguous step definitions can cause false “completed” state (reduces trust).
- Dashboard lag will be interpreted as “usage missing” unless we explicitly set expectations in step copy.
- If we add too many “production” steps, new users may feel overwhelmed. Need tight copy and clear “recommended for production” labeling.

Open questions
- What exact signal defines “env var configured correctly” without client-side instrumentation? Options: derived from first successful request; or mark complete when user views env var docs; or keep as informational (no completion).
- What is the final TTFP definition that’s robust across different customer traffic patterns?
- Do we gate certain production steps (fallback policy, budgets) by plan/tier and show “Learn more” instead of “Configure now”?
- How do we message the checklist to existing tenants without causing confusion or implying something is required?

Decision log (lightweight)
- We will roll out to new tenants first to minimize confusion and measure TTFS cleanly.
- We will prioritize server-side event emission for checklist progress (reliability + PII control).
- Support will have an admin override tool with an audit trail to unblock troubleshooting.

Owner/DRIs

- Hosted API product: Nikhil Sharma
